subject: Clarify SOC 2 Type II coverage & bridge evidence for hosting modes
messages:
From: security@fintechco.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: SOC 2 coverage for hosting modes — Redwood

Hi Stephanie,

Hope you’re well. Quick question from our InfoSec review: we need to confirm whether Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report (for the most recent period) covers the different hosting modes we use: Hosted API (multi-tenant), Dedicated pools (reserved capacity), and Private/VPC (customer-managed VPC or on-prem). Specifically:

- Which hosting models are included in the audited service boundary?
- If Dedicated pools or Private deployments are out of scope, can Redwood provide a bridge letter that describes controls and any compensating evidence?
- What artifacts can we expect to receive to satisfy our SIG/CAIQ review (network diagrams, access control evidence, separation/isolation docs, configuration screenshots, change tickets, etc.)?

Our procurement team also asked about timing — we need a bridge/attestation by early June if possible. Can you confirm feasibility and an initial list of evidence items?

Thanks,
Alex Patterson
InfoSec Manager, FinTechCo
security@fintechco.com

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: security@fintechco.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SOC 2 coverage for hosting modes — Redwood

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list of questions. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

- Hosted API (our managed multi-tenant service) is covered by our latest SOC 2 Type II report (we’ll attach the PDF).
- Dedicated pools: coverage depends on how the dedicated capacity is provisioned and whether it is managed within the same Redwood service boundary. Many of our reserved/dedicated customers are included when the dedicated GPU pool is operated by Redwood and subject to the same control set — we can confirm on a per-customer basis.
- Private/VPC and on-prem deployments are generally outside the hosted SOC 2 report because customers control networking and some admin functions; for those we provide a bridge letter or attestation that describes the controls Redwood performs plus any expected customer responsibilities.

We can absolutely provide a consolidated evidence package to support SIG/CAIQ items. Typical artifacts we can provide:
- SOC 2 Type II report PDF (attached)
- Hosting boundary statement (scoped list of services/configs in/out of the report)
- Network diagram for Hosted and Dedicated (where applicable)
- Example config screenshots and hardening checklist for Dedicated pools
- KMS/HSM architecture note and key ownership statement for Private/VPC customers
- Sample logs retention policy and a small sample of redacted logs for verification
- Change management and patching tickets (redacted)

Timeline: I can share a draft bridge letter and an evidence checklist by the end of day Monday, 1 June, and a complete evidence bundle within 5 business days after we confirm the exact scope (i.e., whether your Dedicated pool is operated by Redwood).

Would you and procurement be available for a 30-minute call Monday afternoon to align scope? I’ll loop in Karthik (security & compliance) and Laura (audit owner) so they can weigh in.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: maria.lopez@compliancefirm.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: security@fintechco.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SOC 2 coverage for hosting modes — Redwood

Hi Stephanie — Maria here from ComplianceFirm (the external assessor engaged by FinTechCo). A few clarifying questions so we can map items to SIG/CAIQ controls and avoid follow-ups:

1) For Dedicated pools said to be "operated by Redwood": can you confirm whether they are logically tenant-isolated (separate tenancy per customer) or rely on strict access controls on shared infrastructure? Any short architecture note would help.

2) For Private/VPC deployments: will Redwood maintain any customer-side agents that require access to customer networks? If so, what controls are in place for that access (MFA, IP allowlists, ephemeral creds)?

3) Do you retain separate audit logs for Dedicated pools tied to customer IDs (for example, admin actions, configuration changes)? If yes, what is the retention period and format?

4) Please list the exact artifact filenames you will provide (we prefer a folder with: SOC2 PDF, hosting-boundary.pdf, network-diagram-hosted.pdf, network-diagram-dedicated.pdf, kms-architecture.pdf, logs-sample.zip, change-tickets-redacted.pdf).

Finally, FinTechCo requested a bridge letter that covers the 30-day gap between your last audit period and our planned go-live. Is Redwood able to provide an attestation that references the same control sets, with a dated signature from your compliance lead and the external auditor? If an external auditor signature is required, please let us know who we should expect to sign.

Thanks — if you can respond by EOD Monday we can keep our assessment timeline.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Senior Assessor, ComplianceFirm
maria.lopez@compliancefirm.com

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: maria.lopez@compliancefirm.com, security@fintechco.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SOC 2 coverage for hosting modes — Redwood

On Sun, May 30, 2026 at 14:20, maria.lopez@compliancefirm.com wrote:
> Hi Stephanie — Maria here from ComplianceFirm (the external assessor engaged by FinTechCo). A few clarifying questions so we can map items to SIG/CAIQ controls and avoid follow-ups:
> 
> 1) For Dedicated pools said to be 'operated by Redwood': can you confirm whether they are logically tenant-isolated (separate tenancy per customer) or rely on strict access controls on shared infrastructure? Any short architecture note would help.

Thanks for the questions — answers below and next steps at the bottom.

1) Dedicated pools operated by Redwood are provisioned as isolated GPU node groups within our orchestration cluster. We use logical isolation (namespace/tenant ID) + network segmentation and per-tenant access controls. For particularly sensitive deployments we can offer additional dedicated hardware assignment; we will call out the exact flavor in the hosting-boundary.pdf.

2) For Private/VPC: Redwood may run a small connector (outbound-only) for metrics/health telemetry if customers opt into Redwood-managed monitoring. That connector uses mTLS with customer-provided certs; no inbound access is required. Where access is needed for remediation, it is executed through an ephemeral session broker and logged — MFA and RBAC enforced.

3) Audit logs: yes — for Dedicated pools we retain admin and control-plane logs tagged by tenant ID for 365 days by default. Logs can be exported in JSON/CSV format; we will provide a redacted sample (logs-sample.zip).

4) Artifact filenames we will provide in the evidence bundle: 
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-2026.pdf
- hosting-boundary.pdf
- network-diagram-hosted.pdf
- network-diagram-dedicated.pdf
- kms-architecture.pdf
- logs-sample.zip
- change-tickets-redacted.pdf

Bridge letter: we can provide a dated bridge letter signed by our Director of Compliance (me). If FinTechCo requires an external auditor co-signature, Redwood will coordinate with AuditPartners (eric.hughes@auditpartners.com) to obtain a signing attestation — that process usually takes 2–3 business days after we share the final draft. I will attach a draft bridge-letter-draft.docx to this thread.

Next steps / timeline:
- Monday EOD (1 Jun): draft bridge letter and the evidence checklist (evidence-checklist.csv) — attached.
- Within 5 business days after scope confirmation: full evidence bundle (PDFs and redacted logs).
- If external auditor signature required: 2–3 business days to obtain co-signature after draft finalization.

Please confirm scope (whether your Dedicated pool is Redwood-operated) and we’ll proceed. Happy to jump on the call Monday afternoon if you’d like — suggest 2pm PT.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-2026.pdf (pdf), evidence-checklist.csv (csv), bridge-letter-draft.docx (docx)
